sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C19
sources.note: Survey-wide disclaimer, sec. 1.3.3 p. 7: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Samosa (SAM) is only an 'additional member' of the Hanseman Family (fn. 9, p. 42: 'included only in the population figures, but will be disregarded in other respects'); sec. 2.21.12.24 (p. 44): 'Villages: Samosa, Soli. Previously unrecorded.' No Samosa forms in the book.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide (The World of Linguistics 4), 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. (Open-access chapter; OAPEN handle 20.500.12657/23719.)
sources.note: For Samosa the chapter records only speaker number and that the sole documentation is Z'graggen's 1980 wordlist. Section 2.4.3 'Prosody' (pp. 88-89) surveys tone/pitch accent/stress across TNG (Donohue 1997, Ross 2005b typology; word tone in East Kewa, Kairi; contrastive stress in Koiarian and Baraic; 'Detailed descriptions of TNG pitch accent systems are lacking') with no statement about Samosa, Hanseman, Mabuso or Croisilles prosody.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. xvi+184+10 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-D32
sources.note: Nothing. Samosa = C13 (346-item list + pronoun/affix table p. 167). Intro sec. 6 (p. viii): 'The transcription is semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted and fluctuating sounds were transcribed consistently only when discovered early enough' -- discusses stop voicing, labio-velars, nasalised vowels, per-language fluctuations (Samosa not listed); no word 'stress', 'accent' or 'tone' anywhere. Visual check of printed pp. 2, 136, 144: C13 forms (sagogu 'old', na 'child', fu- 'blow', kar~- 'dig', mur~a- 'kill', evo- 'fight') carry length and r-tilde but no stre…
